correctness.rationale: In characteristic 3, e4(x+t·1) equals e4(x) on the sum-zero hyperplane, yielding a genuine quartic on a four-dimensional quotient and a projective cone. Fifteen explicit pair-difference classes are distinct singular base points. On a symmetry-complete affine chart the exact reduced lex Groebner basis has nine standard monomials and nine distinct rational zeros, exhausting all geometric chart singularities; the Hessian determinant at each is 1 modulo 3, proving ordinary nodes. S5 symmetry gives exactly fifteen base nodes; the cone has exactly fifteen ruling singular lines. Finite singular set forces the quartic base to be geometrically integral, while hypersurface S2 and regular codimension 1 prove normality of base and cone. The executable exact checker recomputes the coefficient and local certificates. The 76-point finite count is explicitly only corroborative.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: An isolated 45-node quartic in characteristic 0 supplies no flat assertion about singular schemes in characteristic 3. The five-coordinate bad-special-fibre equation does not imply the normal six-coordinate special fibre because the change of models is not invertible modulo 3. The classical Igusa quartic also has fifteen singular lines, but is a different member of the quartic pencil and those lines are not fifteen concurrent lines. The new conclusion requires explicit characteristic-three quotient and Jacobian-scheme computations.

originality.rationale: The classical characteristic-zero 45-node Burkhardt geometry, defining symmetric quartic and five-coordinate rational model are acknowledged antecedents. The reviewed statement is instead the complete fifteen-node base and fifteen-line singular star for the coefficientwise characteristic-three fibre of the specified six-coordinate integral model, including its integrality and normality. Bruin–Nasserden exclude characteristic 3, and their alternative equation degenerates to a reducible nonreduced equation modulo 3. The general characteristic-zero literature does not logically imply a singular configuration in bad characteristic. Source comparison is qualified because one original 1990 paper was not fully accessible.

An unindexed modular-forms account may identify the same symmetric characteristic-three integral model and its fifteen nodal base points.

value.rationale: The Burkhardt quartic is a distinguished modular quartic whose characteristic-three reduction is not governed by its characteristic-zero 45-node geometry. A specified natural symmetric integral model stays normal and integral while acquiring fifteen concurrent one-dimensional singular strata, opposite in scheme-theoretic behavior to the familiar nonreduced five-coordinate reduction. This exactly determines its reduced singular geometry and a canonical fifteen-nodal quartic base, information relevant to comparing compactifications/integral models and studying singular degenerations; it is neither a point-count nor a routine consequence of a changed parameter.
